name: Metformin + Vildagliptin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Both components depend on the kidneys: metformin is excreted unchanged and accumulates (lactic acidosis risk), and vildagliptin exposure rises. The European label caps metformin at 2,000 mg/day at glomerular filtration rate (GFR) 45–59 and 1,000 mg/day at GFR 30–44, with vildagliptin 50 mg/day in both bands, and contraindicates the combination below GFR 30 mL/min. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: European summary of product characteristics (SmPC) uses glomerular filtration rate (GFR, mL/min); bands shown as eGFR.

bands.recommendation: GFR ≥90: usual dose, one tablet (50/850 or 50/1000 mg) twice daily with meals; vildagliptin maximum 100 mg/day. GFR 60–89: metformin maximum 3,000 mg/day, consider reduction as function declines; no vildagliptin change (SmPC).

GFR 45–59: metformin maximum 2,000 mg/day (start at no more than half the maximum); vildagliptin 50 mg/day. GFR 30–44: metformin maximum 1,000 mg/day (start at no more than half); vildagliptin 50 mg/day. Because vildagliptin is capped at 50 mg/day, use one tablet daily or the single agents (SmPC). Note: the combination tablet caps vildagliptin at GFR <60 per its own table (Eucreas), whereas Galvus alone changes at CrCl <50.
GFR <30: contraindicated (SmPC). Use the single agents (vildagliptin 50 mg once daily) instead.

hd.text: Contraindicated (metformin; GFR <30). Vildagliptin alone may be used at 50 mg once daily (see vildagliptin).

crrt.text: Not appropriate: contraindicated in severe kidney impairment and acute conditions that may alter kidney function (SmPC).

dialyzable: Metformin: yes, hemodialysis is the most effective way to remove it in overdose. Vildagliptin: not removed meaningfully; its main inactive metabolite is (SmPC 4.9).
monitoring: GFR before starting and at least yearly; every 3 to 6 months in older adults and those at risk of progression. Stop before or at the time of iodinated contrast. Stop at the time of surgery under general, spinal or epidural anesthesia; restart no earlier than 48 hours after surgery or after oral intake resumes, once kidney function is stable. Hold on sick days (vomiting, diarrhea, dehydration). Liver function tests at baseline, every 3 months in year 1, then periodically (SmPC 4.4).
